minutes_text:
ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES
  July 31, 2017

1. CALL TO ORDER

  CHAIRWOMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m.

2. ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Mitchell, Giglia, Chan-Southwell, Krieger, Larson,
  Stegura, Vona, Radocchio

  Committee Members Absent:  Warner

  Staff Members Present:  Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager
  Jeannie Naughton, Sr. Planner

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A. ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2016

  COMMITTEE MEMBER GIGLIA MADE A MOTION AND SECONDED BY COMMITTEE
  MEMBER LARSON TO APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2016.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MITCHELL so ordered.

4. AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  None

5. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ELECTRICAL VEHICLE CHARGING STATION USAGE FEE

  Staff Member Davis summarized the staff report on Electrical Vehicle (EV) Charging Station
  Usage Fees. The City purchase its first EV and approved a contract to install a new charging
  station at City Hall. Staff Member Davis explained that the station has a dual port with one to
  be used for the City vehicle and the other for the public and provided a brief presentation on
  details on the system and usage fee options. Staff Member Davis stated that the City has
  worked with ChargePoint on an analysis to determine options for a rate structure.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER RADICCHIO asked if two vehicles are using the charging station,
  would they still charge in three hours. Staff Member Davis responded, yes, for a full charge.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER GIGLIA asked who conducted the analysis. Staff Member Davis
  stated that the information was compiled by ChargePoint and took into account the fees
  charged by SCE and other administrative/maintenance costs.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA asked if it should first be determined who will be using
  the charging stations and asked if there could be an additional option to provide the charging
  station at a small amount of time as a public service and use savings in other areas to offset
  the cost. Staff Member Davis stated that cities are moving away from this practice as it could
  be considered a gift of public funds, but this could be further explored. Staff Member Davis
  stated that staff has discussed offering discounted Holiday rates.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VONA stated that as more people are purchasing EV’s, the issue of
  people using them for extended periods of time could become a problem and stated that a
  time limit would be important.

Environmental Advisory Committee
Meeting Minutes, July 31, 2017
   COMMITTEE MEMBER KRIEGER stated that a problem she has come across is vehicles
  parked at EV stalls long after use of the charging station and suggested that the City should
  prepare for ways to handle enforcement of these types of situations.

  Staff Member Davis stated that City Hall does not get a lot of traffic.

  Staff Member Naughton stated that if charging stations are shown on an APP, then it may
  attract more people to City Hall.

  CHAIR MITCHELL stated that the issue of enforcement can be revisited if it becomes a
  problem.

  CHAIR MITCHELL stated that the installation of the station provides expanded charging
  opportunities and will not only be a service for the residents but also to others who pass
  through the City.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER GIGLIA suggested, if the station gets a lot of users, there should be
  consideration to install at various other locations throughout the City, such as parks and
  shopping centers.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER RADICCHIO suggested a 6-month trial period.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER KRIEGER suggested that the City promote the option chosen as a
  pilot program and reconsider if adjustments are needed.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER GIGLIA made a motion, and seconded by CHAIR MITCHELL to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO COUNCIL TO APPROVE THE EV CHARGING STATION
  USAGE FEE AT $0.25 / KWH + $0.50 SERVICE CHARGE AND A MAXIMUM OF 3 HRS.

  There being no objection, CHAIR Mitchell so ordered.

  B. CITY-OWNED STREETLIGHT LED RETROFIT

  Staff Member Davis summarized the staff report on the proposed City-owned streetlight LED
  retrofit project. She stated that LED’s deliver better light, cost savings, lower maintenance
  cost, and have a longer life. Staff Member Davis stated that an assessment was done of
  SCE- owned and City-owned street lights; 55 streetlights are identified to be City-owned. This
  project will reduce energy consumption by 67%. This project has an upfront investment of
  $35K and an estimated cost savings of $5,000 per year. SCE offers interest free loans but
  the payback schedule is different from the time it would take the City to pay back the loan from
  cost savings, thus 10% or $3,300 will need to be paid upfront.

  CHAIR MITCHELL stated that changing the traffic signals to LED provided a dramatic cost
  savings.

  COMMITTEE RADICCHIO inquired on the streetlights owned by SCE. Staff Member Davis
  stated that she will provide the information at the next meeting.

  Staff Member Davis stated that SCE may retrofit the SCE-owned streetlights within the City
  and this will also benefit the City in cost savings since the City pays the bill for SCE-owned
  streetlights within the City.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CHAN-SOUTHWELL asked when SCE will retrofit their streetlights.
  Staff Member Davis stated that ideally all lights will be changed at the same time, but cannot
  say for sure.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER LARSON made a motion, and COMMITTEE MEMBER GIGLIA
  seconded the motion to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL THAT THE CITY PURSUE
  RETROFITTING ALL CITY-OWNED STREETLIGHTS WITH MORE EFFICIENT LED LAMPS.

Environmental Advisory Committee
Meeting Minutes, July 31, 2017
   There being no objection, CHAIR MITCHELL so ordered.

6. OLD BUSINESS

  A. COMMUNITY CHOICE AGGREGATION UPDATE

  Staff Member Naughton provided background and a report on the Community Choice
  Aggregation (CCA) program. She explained the CCA is an energy supplying model that works
  with the existing utility infrastructure. AB117 and AB790 authorized the creation of CCA
  programs which allows local governments to purchase power on the wholesale market and
  sell it to the residents and businesses at competitive rates. CCA’s are non-profit and set their
  rates to cover their costs and reinvests any profits back to the program to keep rates low and
  to invest in small scale energy production sites. In 2015 Los Angeles County began a
  feasibility study which completed in 2016 and made the decision to move forward with the
  program. The Board of Supervisors authorized the County to pursue the creation of LACCA
  and $10 million to start-up the program. Rolling Hills Estates was the first City to participate
  in the creation of the LACCA. Residents will have options to choose levels at which
  percentage they would like their energy to come from renewable sources.

  Staff Member Naughton stated that the program will be phased as follows: Phase 1 in January
  2018 will include LA County municipal facilities in the unincorporated areas and any
  participating cities that are in the programs municipal facilities; Phase 2 in July 2018 will
  include residents in the unincorporated areas; Phase 3 in 2019 will include all participating
  cities. Staff Member Naughton stated that 60 days prior to the roll-out of the program, the City
  will send out four notices to all customers in Rolling Hills Estates giving them the option to opt-
  out of the program.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER KRIEGER asked if residents will have the option to opt-in or opt-out
  of the program anytime. Staff Member Naughton stated that that it her understanding.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER GIGLIA asked about residents using solar. Staff Member Naughton
  stated that she will have to check with LACCA about any over-energy incentive. She added
  that the state has required that City’s streamline their approval process and charge no more
  than $500 for permits.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER RADICCHIO asked if SCE will take care of any damage to equipment.
  Staff Member Naughton stated that everything will remain the same as far as who to call for
  electrical issues and billing.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA asked if there would be any issues if too many people opt
  out of the program. Staff Member Naughton stated that is a cause of concern; if an insufficient
  number of people participate, the City can be dropped from the program and incur nominal
  administrative fees.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER KRIEGER asked if there are will be any protections in place for
  consumers. Staff Member Davis stated that this program, same as SCE, is regulated by the
  Public Utilities Commission (PUC).

  Staff Member Naughton stated that the first board meeting of the LACCA will be this Friday.

  B. DROUGHT UPDATE AND CITY RESPONSE

  Staff Member Davis summarized the staff report on the Drought Update and City Response.
  She provided background on the water restrictions that were previously approved and stated
  that the City has tried to stay consistent with CalWater.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA inquired about enforcement mechanisms for those
  violating water restrictions. Staff Member Davis stated that Code Enforcement has addressed
  storm water run-off violations. She stated Code Enforcement responds to reported code
  violations.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER GIGLIA made a motion, and seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  RADICCHIO to,

Environmental Advisory Committee
Meeting Minutes, July 31, 2017
   Recommend to the City Council to reduce the City’s conservation level from Level 2 to Level
  1 to be consistent with CalWater.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MITCHELL so ordered.

  C. ENERGY UPDATE

  Staff Member Davis provided a brief update on what the City is doing in regards to Energy
  Conservation. She stated that the City has reached the Gold tier on the Energy Leader
  Partnership Program (ELP), which provides a 13 cents per kWh savings incentive to the City.
  The streetlight project will likely put the City at the Platinum tier. Staff Member Davis stated
  that most recently various City facilities upgraded lighting to LED and it was done at no cost
  to the City. This will provide for an annual cost savings of $1,100.

7. DISCUSSION ITEMS

8. COMMITTEE ITEMS (VERBAL REPORTS)

  CHAIR MITCHELL stated that under SB375, the community is required to reduce energy
  usage. The program helps cities and municipalities reduce emissions. Staff Member Davis
  stated a future agenda item will be the Climate Action Plan and Land Use and Transportation.

9. STAFF ITEMS (VERBAL REPORTS)

  A. NEW AGENDA PACKET PROCESS

  Staff Member Davis stated that agendas may be viewed through the Granicus website and
  offered the EAC the option to receive a login and password to access the site as an alternate
  way to receive future agenda packets.

  B. PROGRAMS AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC

  Staff Member Davis provided information on the various programs that are being offered from
  other organizations to residents of RHE including the HERO Program, for which Staff Member
  Davis provided the EAC with a map showing how many residents have used the program.

10. COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None

11. ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR MITCHELL adjourned the meeting at 8:52 p.m.

Environmental Advisory Committee
Meeting Minutes, July 31, 2017
